subject: MAP: performance report and discrepancy analysis for Finvera evaluation
messages:
From: Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwood.com>
To: Alex Jensen <alex.jensen@finvera.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Sergio Alvarez <sergio_alvarez@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 1 Apr 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: MAP milestone: initial performance report and next steps

Alex / Team,

Following up on our MAP milestone (Evaluation: performance validation) — attached is the first pass of the perf report we ran against the Finvera baseline workload. Key highlights up front:

- Test config: Redwood hosted, gpt-x-small-v1 (quantized), sequence length 512 prompt + 256 generation, 8xA10 equivalent, client requests simulated from us-east-1.
- Throughput (tokens/s): 18k sustained at concurrency=16 (batching enabled).
- Latency (TTFT): median TTFT 210ms, P95 TTFT 620ms (single-request path).
- Step latency (per-token generation): P50 12ms / P95 42ms.
- Cold-start behavior: first-token latency ~1.1s on a cold container.

Attached: finvera-map-perf-results.csv (summary + raw traces), finvera-mAP-v1.2.pdf (MAP snapshot we shared).

Next steps we propose in the MAP:
1) You to confirm the workloads (prompts + sampling settings) we used match your evaluation set.
2) If you see mismatches, share a redacted sample and we’ll reproduce inside the same test harness.
3) Schedule a 45min triage call with our infra engineer to walk through traces — proposed: Thu 2026-04-02 10:00 PT.

If these numbers look broadly aligned, we’ll draft a performance SLA block for the Dedicated offer in the MAP. If not, we want to hit parity on methodology first.

Thanks,
Connor O'Brien
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference
--
Redwood Inference

From: Alex Jensen <alex.jensen@finvera.com>

Cc: Finvera Evaluation Team <eval-team@finvera.com>, procurement@finvera.com
Date: Thu, 2 Apr 2026 08:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: MAP milestone: initial performance report and next steps

Connor,

Thanks for the quick turn. A few immediate observations from our side after a quick sweep:

- Our internal numbers show TTFT median closer to ~120ms and P95 ~300ms for roughly the same prompt set using our benchmarking harness (k6 + grpc client). That’s materially faster than your P95.
- We also see higher cold-start spikes (~900ms) occasionally but not as frequent as your traces suggest.

Potential differences we suspect:
- Client-side batching and pipeline settings (we use a concurrent async client + client-side batching).
- Tokenization differences (we use a customized tokenization wrapper that merges a preprocessing step).
- Test harness: we are running across eu-west-1 -> us-east-1 cross-region network hops for a portion of runs.

Can you provide the exact harness, request patterns, and the seed prompts we should run to reproduce your CSV? Procurement is watching the MAP timeline and we need to align on methodology before we commit.

Alex Jensen
Director, Platform Engineering | Finvera

Team — forwarding Alex’s reply. Procurement at Finvera is gating next week’s decision on alignment of methodology. Alex’s P95 numbers are materially lower than ours; they run a different harness and possibly client-side batching.

Proposed internal triage steps (short):
1) Re-run our CSV with the exact prompts we used but remove server-side batching (force batch size = 1) to mirror a single-conn async client.
2) Run identical tests from eu-west-1 to emulate their cross-region traffic.
3) Provide a minimal repro harness (single script + Dockerfile) and a step-by-step playbook. I sketched one — attaching redwood-repro-playbook.md.
4) If numbers still differ, run comparative trace with their team on a joint call (screen-share) and compare request/response headers + tokenization outputs.

Evelyn, can you lead the repro runs and confirm how much time we need? Marissa/Sergio — flag any expected infra cost for cross-region repeated runs.

Connor

From: Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.com>
To: Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Sergio Alvarez <sergio_alvarez@redwood.com>, Alex Jensen <alex.jensen@finvera.com>
Date: Tue, 7 Apr 2026 10:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Repro results and notes — Finvera MAP perf reconciliation

Alex / Connor / Team,

I ran the repro matrix this morning using the playbook. Quick summary of findings:

Test matrix executed:
- Client modes: (A) async single-request (batch=1) from eu-west-1, (B) client-side batching (k=8) from us-east-1, (C) server-side batching (Redwood default) from us-east-1.
- Model variant: gpt-x-small-v1 quantized (same weight).
- Prompts: 120 redacted samples from your set (seeded).

Results (median TTFT / P95 TTFT):
- Mode A (single-request, eu-west-1): median 130ms / P95 310ms — aligns closely with Finvera’s internal numbers.
- Mode B (client batching k=8): median 150ms / P95 340ms.
- Mode C (server batching): median 210ms / P95 620ms — reproduces our original CSV.

Takeaway: the major delta is batching policy. Our default test harness exercised server-side batching which increases per-request TTFT under low concurrency, whereas Finvera’s harness performs client-side async single requests, which gives better tail behavior for their workload. Tokenization differences were negligible after we ran the same tokenizers. Cross-region adds ~10–20ms median and ~30–40ms on tails, not the primary delta.

Actions proposed:
- Update the MAP to include a canonical test mode that matches Finvera’s production client: async single-request from eu-west-1 (Mode A). We will regenerate the perf document following that mode.
- Add an appendix that shows server-side batching tradeoffs (throughput vs TTFT) so Finvera can decide the Desired SLO.
- Joint call to review appendix and agree on which mode is the acceptance criteria. Suggested time: Fri 2026-04-09 11:00 PT.

I’ll attach the raw traces and the run commands to the Drive link and have the regenerated CSV by EOD.

— Evelyn
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

- Performance baseline (Mode A, reproduced): median TTFT 128ms, P95 TTFT 315ms, throughput 9k tokens/s at concurrency=8.
- Appendix included: server-side batching tradeoffs and Dedicated sizing guidance (expected throughput gains and median TTFT penalties).
- Docs: repro playbook + raw traces uploaded to https://drive.redwood.com/finvera/perf-repro-playbook (links archived in MAP).
